assessment.task: Per-scale harness deadline for the 200% native window gate (ADR-WINDOW-SCALE2-DEADLINE-20261112)
assessment.summary: 41/100 stays 41/100. CI harness hardening only: scale 1 keeps the preregistered 1800 s bound and scale 2 may use 2700 s on slower hosted runners, after two scale-2 timeouts on main 49f80b1e (run 43137766280); no phase or assertion changes and no product criterion changes. Merged with main a60425ab (#313, #315, #320; no criterion change).

gates.title: Independent UEFI boot
gates.acceptance: The custom loader transfers control to the custom kernel; normal boot, missing/corrupt kernel, and timeout cases are checked natively.

gates.title: Independent memory management and fault boundaries
gates.acceptance: Custom page tables and frame management, W^X, guard stacks, and invalid mappings are checked in the fixed QEMU profile.

gates.title: Isolated preempted processes
gates.acceptance: Ring-3 processes have separate address spaces; an application fault does not stop the other test processes.

gates.title: Capabilities and bounded IPC
gates.acceptance: Rights reduction, generations, revocation, user-copy handling, and bounded Message320 IPC have native negative and lifecycle tests.

gates.title: General process and service management
gates.acceptance: Non-fixture applications can start and stop through bounded APIs and services can restart; dependencies and resources are released correctly.

gates.title: Multiple processor cores
gates.acceptance: SMP scheduling, synchronization, interrupts, and address-space switching work under concurrent load on the supported profile.

gates.title: Resource management under pressure
gates.acceptance: Memory, CPU, IPC, and handle exhaustion remain bounded per application; the usable system recovers without kernel failure.

gates.title: Native read, write, and flush
gates.acceptance: Service-bound READ/WRITE/FLUSH operations use real virtio I/O; success is reported only after controlled completion.

gates.title: Journal and cold recovery
gates.acceptance: A bounded object journal survives native interruptions, revision checks, full storage, and cold recovery with an independent disk oracle.

gates.title: Names and domain-bound catalog
gates.acceptance: Native GET/PUT/DELETE/RENAME/LIST preserve names, contents, and domain boundaries, including interrupted renames.

gates.title: Space reuse and scalable volumes
gates.acceptance: Storage safely reuses deleted space and continues beyond the former 32-record limit; crash-consistent compaction and quotas are tested.

gates.title: Documents of useful size
gates.acceptance: Large documents and streams exceed the former 128-byte probe limit; bounded buffers, full volumes, and partial writes are tested.

gates.title: Collections, metadata, and edit history
gates.acceptance: Native object collections, persistent metadata, and recoverable revisions support daily Material tasks with consistent transactions.

gates.title: Uncertain I/O without kernel panic
gates.acceptance: The current M6c catalog service returns controlled Unknown results for native WRITE/FLUSH failures, closes further access, and does not replay uncertain writes; there is no false ACK or kernel panic and other processes remain alive. Fault injection, cold recovery, disk-oracle checks, and normal M6c/M6b regressions are stored. This does not extend the historical M6b observer with a new error-handling claim.

gates.title: General storage recovery after failures
gates.acceptance: A usable system remains responsive during disk failure, timeouts, corruption, and resource exhaustion; explicit recovery choices prevent silent data overwrite.

gates.title: Backup, recovery, and data export
gates.acceptance: A user can create, verify, restore, and export independent recovery copies in documented formats; loss and conflict scenarios are tested.

gates.title: First independent device path
gates.acceptance: Custom virtio block transport, bounded DMA/MMIO access, reset behavior, and driver/service crashes are tested natively in QEMU.

gates.title: Keyboard, mouse, and USB
gates.acceptance: Common input and USB devices work on the documented reference profile; hotplug and invalid device responses remain bounded.

gates.title: Graphics output and audio
gates.acceptance: Native graphics output, required GPU functionality, and audio meet documented usability and latency budgets on physical reference hardware.

gates.title: Network hardware and connections
gates.acceptance: Ethernet, Wi-Fi, and the agreed Bluetooth functions work on supported hardware, including disconnect, resume, and driver-failure paths.

gates.title: Power management and sleep/wake
gates.acceptance: ACPI/power management, sleep/wake, shutdown, and thermal/battery functions are measured and recoverable on supported hardware.

gates.title: Physical support matrix
gates.acceptance: Several predefined representative PC configurations pass the documented hardware matrix; DMA/IOMMU boundaries and limitations are explicit.

gates.title: Native compositor and session
gates.acceptance: The custom kernel runs an interactive graphical session with render and input chains, window/surface isolation, and controlled compositor recovery.

gates.title: Responsive daily interaction
gates.acceptance: Keyboard, pointer, focus, clipboard, and application switching are usable natively and meet measured interaction budgets.

gates.title: Material from open to save
gates.acceptance: Users open, edit, rename, and organize real native documents; permissions, history, and location remain understandable and correct.

gates.title: Native accessibility
gates.acceptance: Keyboard-only use, screen reader support, scaling/zoom, contrast, and reduced motion work in the native chain; user task tests are recorded.

gates.title: Settings, search, and recovery
gates.acceptance: Native system settings, local search, account/session management, and understandable error/recovery paths work consistently.

gates.title: Polish validated with users
gates.acceptance: Representative users complete agreed core tasks; friction, errors, and visual inconsistencies are measured and resolved within product budgets.

gates.title: Native packet and transport stack
gates.acceptance: The operating system's network service processes real packets and bounded IP/TCP/UDP connections; malformed input, backpressure, and shutdown are tested.

gates.title: Configuration and everyday internet
gates.acceptance: Address configuration, name resolution, routes, network transitions, and required internet protocols work on real authorized connections.

gates.title: Native authenticated transport
gates.acceptance: Maintained cryptography/TLS with the documented hybrid PQC choice works natively, including peer verification, negative handshakes, and no silent insecure fallback.

gates.title: Enforceable network permissions
gates.acceptance: Process and destination permissions, revocation, and helper routes are enforced natively and observed in traffic; no unintended listening ports exist.

gates.title: Entropy and key management
gates.acceptance: Native cryptographic entropy and key lifecycle, with recovery restricted to manifest-bound management ingress. Native positive management recovery and negative ordinary-app authorization tests remain required.

gates.title: Authenticated personal storage
gates.acceptance: Content and sensitive metadata are protected natively; tampering, replay/rollback within the threat model, and key loss are tested.

gates.title: Signed updates and rollback
gates.acceptance: Authentic updates, interruption, downgrade attacks, and recovery to a valid previous version are tested end to end.

gates.title: Trusted boot and distribution chain
gates.acceptance: Image/boot verification, key rotation, and dependency/build provenance are bounded for the release profile and independently reviewed.

gates.title: Targeted independent security review
gates.acceptance: External experts examine kernel, service, DMA, parser, and capability boundaries; blocking findings are resolved and selected invariants are machine-checked where appropriate.

gates.title: Native privacy contract
gates.acceptance: Applicable LP tests pass on the independent OS, including no telemetry/cloud fallback, local AI, and separated app/download permissions; remaining risks are published.

gates.title: Publicly documented application API and SDK
gates.acceptance: A reproducible SDK builds ordinary applications for the independent OS; API/ABI versions, sandbox behavior, and errors are documented and tested.

gates.title: Install and update applications
gates.acceptance: Packages from multiple sources can be installed, removed, and updated with provenance checks; installation does not grant broad capabilities.

gates.title: Application permissions and tool integration
gates.acceptance: Native applications use Material objects through visible, revocable task permissions; extensions and helper processes cannot bypass those boundaries.

gates.title: Useful everyday applications
gates.acceptance: At minimum, internet use, document editing, media, and file exchange work through suitable native applications or controlled ports; realistic user tasks are tested.

gates.title: Native end-to-end encrypted NAS storage
gates.acceptance: Client and NAS roles on the independent OS pair with verified identity; names and content are unreadable to the NAS administrator, including failure and attack paths.

gates.title: Automatic synchronization and conflicts
gates.acceptance: Previously authorized peers resume automatically; offline edits, conflicts, and LAN/internet transitions preserve permissions and do not silently lose data.

gates.title: Multiple devices and key lifecycle
gates.acceptance: Devices can be securely added and revoked; key rotation, concurrent writers, and recovery work without vendor key escrow.

gates.title: Offer, revoke, and remove storage
gates.acceptance: The native NAS administrator manages quotas and revokes guest authority/removes local copies without guest consent or decryption keys; old sessions do not revive.

gates.title: Useful local system AI
gates.acceptance: At least the agreed core AI tasks run on the local device with bounded context, separate model downloads, and tested network denial; limited resources never cause silent cloud fallback.

gates.title: Local quantum execution on the independent OS
gates.acceptance: The local simulator/job interface runs natively with quotas, cancellation, and reference circuits; host simulation and physical QPU support remain separately labeled.

gates.title: Installation and accessible recovery
gates.acceptance: A user can install, upgrade, and independently recover the OS on supported hardware using controlled preserve/wipe options; a practical test passes.

gates.title: Long-term stability and performance budgets
gates.acceptance: Predefined duration, workload, energy, memory, latency, and data-integrity budgets are met on physical hardware with no known blocking usability defects.

gates.title: Reproducible release and maintenance
gates.acceptance: Independent reproduction, licenses/SBOM, release and patch policy, responsible reporting channel, support, and applicable accessibility/privacy obligations are concretely arranged.
